output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is mainly an internal problem, not a Haverlow one. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four (27 July), the median time from unloading to reaching a cold chamber rose from about 44 minutes to nearly 4 hours. Pallets wait in an unrefrigerated dock area at 15–17°C. Night-shift write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day-shift rates stayed flat. Trailer data that can't be edited shows Haverlow loads were 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened and were empty by about 23:30. The warm receipt probe readings of 6.5–8°C were logged hours later, at confirmation. The chambers held temperature. A chargeback and volume shift against Haverlow would punish the wrong party and rest on misleading readings. I'm fairly confident in this. Next steps: restore the night team to six, cap dock-to-chamber time and monitor it weekly from scan data, and hold the chargeback. Keep the receiving probe. Separately, ask Corriebank for claim-level data. The rise in their credits coincides with self-certification, but that link is not shown, and some of the credits may be for genuinely warmed product.
